Additionally, the model successfully reproduces the spectral features observed by the MAGIC and VERITAS telescopes, suggesting that the jet's structure and dynamics can be effectively described under these conditions.

The "pre-non-relativistic" parametrization enables a straightforward analytical expansion in the $\sqrt{v/c}$ order for the metric and Christoffel symbols within general relativity. Adopting this approach, we analytically derive the equations of motion for a test particle in the post-Newtonian framework and demonstrate their equivalence with the standard geodesic equation.

This paper introduces a new method for image registration, termed Sparse Iterative Affine Point Distribution Model (SIFT-CPD), which merges the robustness of the Compositional Principal Distributions Difference (CPD) model against outliers with the computational efficiency of Sparse Approximate Procrustes Analysis (SAP). While CPD effectively captures complex statistical distributions, it suffers from high computational costs and vulnerability to noise or domain shifts. Conversely, SAP is computationally efficient but fails when faced with significant intensity variations or local anomalies. To address these limitations, SIFT-CPD applies a sparse approximation of the CPD model to enhance robustness while retaining its core strengths. The method was validated using three-dimensional brain images, demonstrating superior performance over existing techniques, including the CPD model itself, specifically in handling contrast variations and irregularities.

We report the discovery of SDSS J082239.54+304857.19, an eclipsing detached double-degenerate binary system with a 2.6-hour orbital period. Analysis of its optical light curve indicates the presence of two white dwarfs of comparable size, with radii of 0.012 and 0.013 solar radii. Spectroscopic observations reveal that the system's combined spectrum resembles a white dwarf of approximately 0.6 solar masses, exhibiting strong He II emission lines and weak hydrogen features. These findings suggest the system consists of a primary white dwarf around 0.6 solar masses and a secondary white dwarf near 0.55 solar masses. The observed He II emission is likely generated by the interaction of the companion star with the primary's magnetosphere, a phenomenon also seen in single white dwarfs. The system's spectral characteristics imply a white dwarf age of roughly 0.1 to 0.2 billion years.

This study introduces a new framework called UOT-Pooling, which utilizes an optimal transport (OT) approach to enhance network performance. We demonstrate that standard pooling layers can be viewed as approximations of the OT push-forward map and propose replacing them with methods derived from the linearization of the unregularized OT problem. Experiments conducted on both classification and unsupervised representation learning tasks indicate that substitiling conventional pooling with the UOT-Pooling framework significantly boosts classification accuracy. Additionally, we validate the framework's effectiveness in the context of contrastive self-supervised learning.

Seyfert galaxies are defined by the presence of active galactic nuclei (AGN) within spiral hosts. While the primary research focus has been on the physical mechanisms driving these AGNs, the host galaxy's environment may also influence the orientation of the resulting Seyfert nuclei. This study investigates the orientation angles of 111 Seyfert nuclei situated in spiral hosts, utilizing a sample drawn from the spectroscopically classified Seyfert catalog by Kinemane et al. (2002). The analysis reveals that Type 1 and Type 2 Seyfert nuclei exhibit distinct orientation distributions. Specifically, Type 1 Seyfert nuclei are more likely to be found face-on, whereas Type 2 Seyfert nuclei favor edge-on alignments. These findings suggest that the orientation of the central engine is linked to the host's environment, supporting the hypothesis that the orientation of the accretion disk around the supermassive black hole is determined by the angular momentum of the gas within the central kiloparsec.

This study introduces a new formulation of the pointwise 1-type Gauss map, applied specifically to general rotational surfaces in $\mathbb{E}^3$. The authors demonstrate that a general rotational surface possesses a pointwise 1-type Gauss map if and only if it is flat.

Estimating scene geometry is likely a more fundamental pre-training objective than standard image classification. This paper proposes an approach to train a model for monocular depth estimation using only unlabelled data, leveraging a novel self-supervised loss function that measures the consistency of rendered features. We validate the efficacy of this method through extensive experiments, including a detailed analysis of the resulting features and their relationship to scene structure. The study presents a comparison with other self-supervised techniques and evaluates the features' utility for monocular depth estimation and semantic segmentation tasks.

The TCube framework is designed to address the scarcity of annotated time-series data by enabling efficient, cost-effective labeling through the generation of derived samples. It achieves this by creating TCubes—representations of localized, multi-dimensional data segments—across various points in the time-series space. Because these segments are often intuitively understandable, they serve as an ideal basis for labeling. The system supports the creation of labeling templates that guide users in applying labels to multiple data segments simultaneously, thereby streamlining the annotation workflow. Additionally, it offers a "Label Propagation" feature that automatically transfers labels from user-annotated segments to others with similar characteristics. Evaluation across three distinct datasets demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms standard alternative techniques.

Rare transitions involving B mesons, exemplified by $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ and $B^0 \to \mu^+\mu^-$, serve as highly sensitive probes of physics extending beyond the Standard Model. These processes are governed by the same effective Hamiltonian, yet they respond differently to potential new physics mechanisms. Consequently, precise measurements of these channels offer a powerful means of constraining theoretical models. This work presents an updated analysis of $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu-$ and $B^0 \to \mu^+\mu-$ decay rates, incorporating the most recent data from LHCb and experimental results from ATLAS and CMS.

This study examines the one-dimensional Ising model defined on a Cayley tree with branching factor $k=2$. We demonstrate that the transformation group governing this system's evolution is precisely the dihedral group $D_4$, allowing for the derivation of all invariant subspaces corresponding to $D_4$'s irreducible representations. Applying the $q$-trace method within these subspaces, we calculate the free energy of the model.

This work examines the impact of phase-space metrics on the degree of smoothness loss in hyperbolic equation solutions and establishes that the newly proposed "metric of nilpotency" offers superior estimates compared to previously used alternatives.

Japanese word segmentation is a pivotal challenge in Natural Language Processing, and while traditional methods have been extensively studied, this report introduces a new approach leveraging Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent neural networks. We propose a specific framework utilizing bidirectional LSTMs to process surrounding context, paired with a mechanism for aggregating multiple candidate entries. Empirical results indicate that this method surpasses existing state-of-the-art systems in accuracy.

Stack Overflow serves as a widely utilized platform for programmers to seek coding assistance and support. Although the site offers immense value, the frequent posting of basic inquiries and the resulting repetition strain both users and moderators. To address this, we developed an automated system that identifies and suggests relevant external resources—such as official documentation, tutorials, and similar materials—to help users avoid duplicate posts. By leveraging official documentation as the primary shared material, we aim to reduce the volume of redundant questions. Our analysis of 1.2 million posts reveals that the system successfully detects 80% of cases where users share external resources, with official documentation accounting for the majority of these instances.

The vast variety of galaxy rotation curves poses a significant challenge for $\Lambda$CDM cosmology, which predicts that dark matter halos should possess nearly identical profiles. This study investigates whether the diversity in rotation curves stems from variations in dark matter (DM) particle physics. We demonstrate that if an isothermal core exists within the halo, the resulting density profile aligns with the universal rotation curve observed in $\Lambda$CDM simulations. Consequently, the final rotation curve of a galaxy depends primarily on its halo's central DM particle properties. We further show that if the particle cross-section is sufficiently small, the initial density profile naturally forms an isothermal core. Consequently, the diversity in rotation curves can be attributed to a wide range of DM particle interaction cross-sections within different galaxies.

Values are fundamental to human behavior, yet the global climate emergency often fails to inspire sufficient personal action due to a lack of connection to individual value systems. This study introduces a novel framework for automatically deriving personal values based on social media activity, with the specific aim of fostering climate-related motivation. The proposed methodology utilizes the BERT model to identify short-term emotional states from Twitter posts, subsequently applying a Markov Switching Hidden State Model to infer long-term stable traits. The resulting values are matched against established definitions from the ClIO and NEO models to validate accuracy. The system was tested using the "Climate Action" dataset from the 2019 Climate Twitter Hackathon, which contains over 1.5 million tweets. The findings demonstrate that the system successfully detects individual value profiles, showing a strong correlation between identified values and verified user profiles.

In the realm of healthcare natural language processing, tasks such as extracting signs, symptoms, and diagnoses often rely on specialized medical corpora that are costly and difficult to assemble. To bypass this barrier, we trained our symptom extraction model using only generic, publicly available hospital records, demonstrating through experiments on three distinct external datasets that domain generalization significantly boosts performance. Furthermore, we observed that pre-training on extensive unstructured clinical text enhances the model's capabilities even more. Collectively, these findings indicate that developing robust NLP tools for specific medical applications does not necessitate access to task-specific annotated data.

This study introduces a novel approach to autonomous driving by integrating Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) into an end-to-end deep learning framework. This method addresses the challenges of state estimation in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) without requiring explicit state estimation. Specifically, the proposed architecture leverages RNNs to maintain a dynamic state representation, thereby enhancing the system's capacity to handle hidden states. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that this technique significantly boosts performance compared to non-recurrent counterparts, particularly in complex scenarios characterized by occlusions and missing data.

Although conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs) dominate classification tasks, their high energy usage limits their viability in resource-constrained environments. In contrast, quantum-classical hybrid models have recently emerged as a promising alternative, featuring low power requirements and strong resistance to overfitting. This study introduces the use of quantum-classical hybrid models as efficient, low-power general classifiers by benchmarking their accuracy against standard ANNs on the MNIST dataset. We specifically evaluate the performance of the quantum-classical model using the Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) architecture, comparing it with fully connected ANNs. Results indicate that these hybrid models achieve accuracy comparable to ANNs on MNIST while maintaining significantly lower power consumption, establishing them as a viable solution for resource-limited applications.

This study examines the impact of a strong magnetic field on the equation of state (EOS) of spin-polarized strange quark matter (SQM). We analyze two models: the MIT bag model and the mass-variable bag model. Our findings indicate that a robust magnetic field significantly alters the MIT EOS, causing a marked softening. Additionally, we calculate the critical magnetic field strength required to initiate spin polarization within the MIT framework.

Personal devices like laptops and smartphones possess untapped potential for executing distributed computations, yet their usage is often restricted by devices' limited processing power and short battery life. To address this, we propose "Pando," a virtual machine designed to distribute workloads efficiently across multiple personal gadgets. Our evaluation demonstrates that a cluster of 100 Android units running Pando achieves a 2.5x increase in computational throughput compared to a single personal device, while also extending the available runtime by a factor of 2.5.

This study introduces a novel adaptive sampling strategy tailored for the finite element approximation of eigenvalues associated with the Laplace eigenproblem on surfaces. By concentrating mesh refinement in areas exhibiting high oscillation of the eigenfunction, the method enhances both the efficiency and accuracy of the numerical solution. The proposed framework is validated through various experiments involving meshes of varying topological complexities, alongside an analysis of its computational efficiency.

This study examines the survivor sets of intermediate $\beta$-transformations and demonstrates that they correspond precisely to the set of badly approximable numbers in non-integer bases, characterized by a common unique digit constraint. Furthermore, the paper establishes the existence of a homeomorphism between these sets; under this mapping, the measure-theoretic entropy of the resulting dynamics in the image set corresponds exactly to the $\beta$-Minkowski dimension of the survivor set for the corresponding transformation.

We establish that the symmetry $SU(N_{F})$ associated with chiral symmetry is explicitly broken in $SO(N_{c})$ gauge theories due to the existence of quark bilinears that are antisymmetric in their $SO(N_{c})$ indices. Consequently, the residual flavor symmetry reduces to the subgroup of $U(1)\times SO(N_{F})$. Our analysis further demonstrates that the vacuum expectation value of the baryon operator vanishes, implying that the system resides in the symmetric phase with respect to the remaining $SO(N_{F})$ symmetry.

This paper introduces a novel method for analyzing deep learning models in time series contexts through the use of Disentangled Attribution Curves. By disentangling temporal features, this approach offers deeper insights into model predictions. We validate the method's efficacy using the bike-sharing dataset, uncovering distinct patterns in weather, station, and historical data. Additionally, we apply the Disentangled Attribution Curve to a clinical time series, revealing critical insights into a patient's condition.

Although federated learning (FL) offers a promising framework for collaborative model training, existing privacy-preserving methods often struggle with significant limitations, including high computational costs, slow convergence, and diminished accuracy. To address these issues, this paper introduces a new approach that leverages homomorphic encryption alongside a proposed $(2k+1)$-th root extraction technique under the encrypted domain. The suggested method ensures privacy by encrypting model parameters during transmission and significantly reduces the $2k+1$-th root extraction complexity from $O(n)$ to $O(1)$ within the encrypted space. Experimental results indicate that this system not only effectively safeguards sensitive data but also surpasses current state-of-the-art solutions in both training speed and final model accuracy.

This document outlines a solution for evaluating microcontroller drivers, developed through an iterative process that began with a needs assessment and progressed to the creation of both a physical hardware platform and accompanying software. The core of this system is a reconfigurable test board equipped with a microcontroller, a suite of sensors, and various actuators. The accompanying codebase includes a kernel-level framework for drivers and user-space applications designed to facilitate drivers testing on the board. The authors present their implementation by detailing the development of the drivers for the test board and the user-space applications used to validate them.

We present Timeloops, a mechanism for system call (syscall) filtering specifically designed to support applications developed in interpreted languages such as Python and PHP. By leveraging the loops inherent in these environments, Timoloops enables the dynamic generation of specialized syscalls. This approach was validated through the creation of bespoke examples and by adapting existing DroidGuard filters for use with Google Chrome and Firefox.

Recent research indicates that single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data, which typically exists in high-dimensional Euclidean space, can be effectively represented in low-dimensional product space forms. This study demonstrates that utilizing classifiers designed for such spaces yields significant performance gains compared to traditional Euclidean methods when analyzing scRNA-seq datasets. Specifically, we found that a 10-dimensional product space within a Hamming metric surpasses the accuracy of state-of-the-art Euclidean techniques by 10-fold. Furthermore, we present a novel dimensionality reduction technique tailored for product space forms that maintains the structural properties of the space and achieves superior results.

We investigate how stars scatter in the gravitational field of a supermassive black hole (SMBH), considering the influence of the surrounding stellar population. We assume a power-law mass function for these stars and demonstrate that, unlike the standard point-particle approximation, the orbital energy distribution exhibits a distinct dependence on the energy itself. Consequently, we find that low-energy stars experience significantly less scattering than their high-energy counterparts. We further examine how these findings modify the standard formula for the rate of energy change for inspiraling compact objects.

Stochastic Model Predictive Control (MPC) addresses system uncertainty by integrating probabilistic constraints into the control framework. This study investigates the relationship between the computational burden of Stochastic MPC and the degree of system uncertainty. The analysis demonstrates that as uncertainty rises, the feasible region for probabilistic constraints expands, thereby increasing the proportion of the state space where the MPC optimization problem remains solvable. Building on this insight, a novel approach to enhancing the efficiency of Stochastic MPC is proposed. This method leverages the deterministic MPC solution as a robust initial guess for the Stochastic MPC optimization, significantly accelerating convergence. The effectiveness of this technique is validated through numerical simulations.

This study addresses Independent Component Analysis (ICA) in compressed domains, specifically targeting the reconstruction of high-dimensional sources from highly compressed mixtures. We introduce two compressive ICA algorithms that require only a fraction of the memory traditionally demanded by full-dimensional ICA while maintaining identical performance. Additionally, we propose a novel, fully unsupervised pre-training method for deep autoencoders. This method relies on the outputs of an ICA process restricted to highly compressed data, eliminating the need for labeled data. We further demonstrate that this pre-training strategy significantly enhances the resilience of autoencoders to corrupted inputs.

This study examines an asymmetric noisy voter model involving two species competing within a finite population, where each individual adopts the opinion of a randomly selected neighbor with a species-dependent bias. When the competitive advantage is held by a single species (asymmetry), the interaction results in either the total dominance of that stronger species or a stable coexistence of both. In contrast, under perfectly balanced competition (symmetry), only random fixation occurs. The analysis focuses primarily on the asymmetric scenario, where the weaker species faces extinction; however, the influence of demographic noise on the absorption time for the declining species is highlighted. The model is further mapped onto a biased random walk framework exhibiting reflection at the origin, allowing for the derivation of a closed-form expression describing the probability distribution of time-to-extinction for the minority species.

This work explores the von Neumann algebras generated by local regions in the thermodynamic limit within a specific class of pure states defined on type $${\rm III}_1$$ von Neumann algebras. These states correspond to the unique ground states of gapped, frustration-free systems consisting of local Type $${\rm III}_1$$ factors. Our findings reveal that the von Neumann algebras associated with these local regions are all of type $${\rm III}_1$$.

We demonstrate that robustness against thermal influences can be achieved through steady-state entanglement in coherent feedback loops. Our analysis indicates that while entanglement produced by standard dissipative coupling to a thermal bath is easily degraded by temperature, the loop-driven coherent feedback preserves this stead-state entanglement even under thermal conditions. We present a specific setup involving two mechanical oscillators connected to a shared optical cavity, which is monitored and processed by an optical detector driving the feedback mechanism. This configuration allows for the generation of entanglement between the oscillators, with the degree of entanglement governed by both the feedback system's properties and the external environment's temperature. Notably, the optimal system parameters for achieving the most thermal-resistant entanglement are distinct from those optimized for the highest feedback efficiency.

We present the first results for massless one-loop triple-collinear splitting operators at the one-loop level. These computed operators serve as the foundation for constructing corresponding subtraction terms in various high-order QCD processes. Furthermore, we demonstrate the splitting operators' universality by showing that their computed forms align with findings from recent studies on multi-loop collinear factorization.

This paper provides an alternative proof of Greenberg's strong approximation theorem for one-dimensional local rings, with utilizations in the formulation of local heights for points of finite order on abelian varieties over function fields.

Preserving and studying historical sundials in Indonesia faces challenges due to a scarcity of data on their locations and designs. To overcome this obstacle, we launched "Cagar Bayang-Bayang Indonesia," a citizen science initiative aimed at crowdsourcing information on Indonesian sundials. This project utilizes a dedicated mobile application to facilitate user-submitted photos and details of sundial artifacts. By employing a Mixture of Experts framework, the initiative leverages input from both the general public and specialists to ensure accurate documentation. Furthermore, the project seeks to educate participants on sundial theory and practice while fostering a broader appreciation for these instruments.

This study introduces a novel Time-Energy-Information Power Splitting (TSIPT) framework for dual-entity, dual-resource (DED2D) scenarios, where a source simultaneously transmits data and energy to a moving receiver equipped with a power splitter. The architecture comprises two components: an information stream directed from the source to the receiver, and an energy stream from the source to a separate energy-harvesting unit (EHU) at the receiver. The EHU converts captured signals into electrical power, which is then allocated to the data decoder. The research evaluates the outage probability and average achievable information rates under Rayleigh fading conditions. Additionally, the optimal power splitting factor is determined to simultaneously minimize outage probability and maximize data throughput. The study further investigates the combined performance of information and energy delivery, specifically analyzing the relationship between the source's total power allocation and the EHU's harvested energy.

Rising demands for teleworking have accelerated the automation of experimental configurations, enabling researchers to conduct intricate work from remote locations. This study examines the advantages and drawbacks of utilizing remote-controlled systems, specifically focusing on a head-mounted display (HMD) robot arm designed for the virtual assembly of tasks. The accompanying analysis evaluates the benefits and limitations of such teleoperation, featuring a study on the teleassembly of head-mounted display robotic arms used in virtual reality.

Asser's conjecture posits that the spectra of undirected graphs form a class closed under the operation of taking subgraphs. In this paper, we investigate an alternative restriction to this problem: limiting the graphs to be undirected and bipartite. Under these conditions, Asser's conjecture is equivalent to the statement that every bipartite graph's spectrum can be decomposed into the sum of two positive definite matrices. By applying the Hadamard product to these matrices, we demonstrate that this equivalence holds. Furthermore, we provide a counterexample to the conjecture when graphs are directed and bipartite.

Electrostatic phase plates (EPPs) serve as highly effective tools for generating phase contrast in transmission electron microscopes, enabling superior image resolution and faster acquisition speeds. This study presents a computational investigation into the EPP's impact on electron probe characteristics, specifically focusing on probe size and current density. Key design variables, including the EPP's fill-factor and pixel configuration, were examined to determine their influence on these metrics. The research confirms that while a larger fill-factor generally enhances current density, achieving minimal probe size necessitates a balanced optimization of both the fill-factor and the pixel pattern. Furthermore, the EPP's position relative to the objective lens was analyzed, with findings indicating that current density is most sensitive to lateral positioning errors, whereas probe size remains largely unaffected by such misalignments.

This study proposes an integrative framework for analyzing the physical mechanisms underlying computation, with a specific focus on quantum computation. We initially outline the fundamental components of this framework and subsequently examine how the mechanism of change, using a concrete example, can be analyzed within it. Furthermore, we demonstrate how to evaluate a quantum computation by applying the framework to a traced qubit operation.

This paper examines the behavior of the random walk in $d$ dimensions, where the walk's step count is restricted to $\lfloor n^{\alpha} \rfloor$ for $0 < \alpha < 1$. It is demonstrated that for dimensions $d \geq 3$, the number of visited positions up to time $\lfloor n^{\alpha} \rfloor$ follows an asymptotic distribution of Gumbel type. Conversely, in dimensions $d=1$ and $d=2$, this count converges weakly to a log-Cauchy distribution. Additionally, the findings address the relationship between the distributions found in dimensions $d$ and their subsequent extension to $d+1$.

This study examines the physical characteristics of a Schwarzschild black hole where the event horizon is constructed from a charged, non-conducting polymer sphere. By applying the modified Randall-Sundrum (RS) model, we demonstrate that this polymer black hole exhibits a superior geometric structure compared to a wormhole, as it more readily satisfies both dominant and null energy conditions. Furthermore, analysis of the surface gravity at the charge-derived horizon reveals that the magnitude of the gravitational field at this boundary is lower than that of a standard Schwarzschild black hole.

We examine the low-energy thermodynamic properties of doped graphene sheets, employing density functional theory to determine the renormalized Fermi velocity and quasiparticle density of states. Our findings indicate that the specific heat capacity scales linearly with temperature, governed by an effective linear dispersion relation characterized by a renormalized quasiparticle velocity. This heat capacity is significantly modified by the inclusion of electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions, which alter the quasiparticle velocity. Additionally, we observe that the density of states exhibits a pronounced logarithmic divergence at the Dirac point, a feature that persists even after incorporating renormalization effects.

We introduce a system for creating natural, expressive, and diverse spoken language by integrating a speech synthesis module with a musical accompaniment generator. This framework, named MaskedSpeech, utilizes a multi-task masked autoencoder to jointly learn the latent representations of both audio elements before employing a masked auto-regressive decoder for end-to-end joint generation. Our experimental results demonstrate that the system outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in quality metrics and successfully produces a wide variety of expressive, natural-sounding speech paired with music.

Variational inference is commonly employed to approximate complex posterior distributions when analytical solutions are unavailable. Although various techniques exist for performing variable selection within Bayesian frameworks, they often struggle to preserve the original posterior uncertainty about model parameters. This study introduces a novel variational approach to variable selection that maintains these critical uncertainties. Specifically, we develop a mask variable selection method utilizing binary masks to achieve this goal. We demonstrate the method's efficacy through experiments on both simulated data and real-world datasets.

Recent studies have demonstrated that Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are vulnerable to "adversarial examples"—inputs with barely perceptible modifications that cause classification errors. While prior research largely examined global or localized attacks targeting a specific sample, this work investigates how such vulnerabilities manifest in Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) scenarios. Unlike previous approaches, our proposed MitM attack operates simultaneously across multiple samples during transmission, effectively bypassing the need for a per-sample gradient query. By exploiting these properties, an adversary can force a DNN to commit classification mistakes on every intercepted packet without requiring gradient access. Our approach successfully deceives DNN classifiers into errors across three distinct real-world applications: image super-resolution, face recognition, and object detection.

Although conspiracy theories about the climate are gaining traction, they remain a niche phenomenon. Our analysis of Twitter data indicates that these theories primarily circulate within organized echo chambers, specifically those linked to anti-vaccine movements and QAnon. These groups function as the central hubs for such narratives, which are only occasionally picked up by mainstream accounts. Consequently, the broader public is largely insulated from these concepts, as the content stays confined to its sources.

This study examines the non-resonant dark matter scenario, where interactions between dark matter and standard model particles occur through off-shell mediators. We employ a statistical framework to analyze constraints on this model derived from direct detection experiments, along with indirect detection and collider searches. Our analysis reveals that existing collider and direct detection limits are largely consistent with one another, particularly for light mediators. Furthermore, we find that current indirect detection bounds are largely complementary to those from direct and collider searches, especially for heavy mediators. By utilizing a Bayesian approach, we establish 95% credible intervals for the dark matter fraction attributed to the $\bar{\chi}\bar{\chi}$-photon off-shell process. Our findings indicate no significant discrepancies from standard model predictions, suggesting dark matter may instead interact via other mechanisms.

This paper introduces a novel framework for exangulated categories, generalizing both exact and Eilenberg-Moore categories. Within this concept, we define an Eilenberg-Moore quiver and demonstrate that any finite-length category equipped with a Q-representation compatible with the structure admits an equivalent representation as an exangulated category. A key result provides necessary and sufficient conditions for Serre duality to exist in such categories, alongside the construction of an alternative representation where Serre duality holds. Finally, we verify that both exact and Eilenberg-Moore categories function as specific instances of the broader exangulated category model.

Earnings returns from post-secondary education are a critical determinant of individual and societal prosperity. This study utilizes a synthetic control method to compare the Norwegian and Danish labor markets, a comparison made feasible by their shared historical roots in post-WWII vocational reforms. The analysis reveals that while Denmark's labor market remains more rigid, the Norwegian market has become increasingly competitive. Furthermore, the research finds that the disparity in earnings across post-secondary majors is significantly wider in Norway than in Denmark, and the disparity is growing over time. Consequently, the competitive Norwegian market offers a more attractive environment for those seeking to maximize educational returns, whereas the relatively less competitive Danish market favors individuals with a stronger preference for job security.

The Super $J/\psi$ factory, a dedicated electron-positron collider designed to operate at center-of-mass energies near the $J/\psi$ resonance, is currently under construction at the Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP) in Beijing. This facility will enable detailed investigations into the properties of the $D$ and $d$-meson systems, as well as the production of charmonium and bottomonium states. Operating with a projected luminosity of $10^{33}~\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, the machine is anticipated to commence data collection in 2022. The proposed design incorporates a compact, cost-effective, and highly efficient $e^+e^-$ collider structure, utilizing a low-$\beta$ collimation system to achieve narrow beam profiles at the interaction zone. This configuration supports precise measurements of cross-sections for narrow resonances and facilitates the study of states with broader widths. Additionally, the design supports operation in a $\tau^+\tau^-$ mode with beam energies around 3.5 GeV, enabling the exploration of top-quark pair production.

We investigate the accretion dynamics of hierarchical triple systems, specifically focusing on the inner binary where two stars interact with a third body in an outer orbit. Our analysis reveals that the smaller component in this inner pair accretes at a rate significantly exceeding that expected for a single star of the same mass, while the larger one accretes more slowly. This phenomenon stems from the inner binary's accelerated rotation induced by the outer companion, which drives a superlinear dependence of mass transfer on the binary's components. Consequently, the mass ratio within the pair evolves rapidly toward equality. Our findings indicate that the total accretion rate of the system is dominated by the star with initially lower mass in the inner binary.

This study investigates the evolution of the universe by extending the Einstein field equations to include inhomogeneous distributions of matter. The analysis demonstrates that initial density variations in the spatial voids lead to the formation of structures. The findings indicate that the universe's overall geometry and expansion rate are influenced by these matter inhomogeneities.

The article introduces a modified version of the piecewise-constant Mumford-Shah model designed to handle image segmentation tasks involving noise. This modification incorporates a non-local self-adjoint term into the model's energy functional, derived from a cost function that quantifies the correlation of image gradients across the entire domain. By integrating this global information, the approach effectively suppresses noise while preserving sharp edges. The corresponding fourth-order partial differential equation is solved using a level-set framework, which is implemented via a fully discrete algorithm. Numerical simulations demonstrate that this methodology yields high-quality segmentation results.

We report the inaugural direct search for dark matter mediated by ultra-light particles through the observation of their oscillations. Our experiment, utilizing a 10 kg germanium detector, is designed to detect time-varying nuclear recoil energies caused by the interaction with oscillating femto-electlectronvolt-scale dark matter particles. The study covers ultra-light particles with masses ranging from $10^{-19}$ to $10^{-14}$ eV/c$^2$ by analyzing a one-year dataset from the detector. Our analysis reveals no statistically significant evidence for such oscillating signals. These findings establish the first direct experimental limits on coupling constants between dark matter and standard model particles in this specific mass and energy regime. Additionally, we investigate ultra-light particles that could interact with dark matter, demonstrating that our results constrain the fraction of dark matter composed of these entities to less than 1% for masses between $10^{-17}$ eV/c$^2$ and $10^{-16}$ eV/c$^2$.

Conventional computing systems separate learning and computing processes, whereas this work introduces the concept of on-chip learning directly within neuromorphic computing arrays. This approach enables the automatic adjustment of internal parameters to adaptively acquire and refine knowledge regarding its environment. The proposed methodology employs a gradient-based technique to optimize weights by leveraging an internal, self-generated surrogate loss function. The paper details the implementation of this training algorithm on an experimental device featuring a 10k array of analog memristive crossbars, which function as the synaptic components. The system was successfully trained to identify handwritten digits using a simplified, unsupervised variant of the MNIST dataset. The successful operation of the device, validated by its ability to perform tasks, highlights the potential of this method for deploying intelligent, adaptive algorithms on emerging neuromorphic hardware platforms.

This study examines a noise storm that originated on 2010 February 15 within the Sun's quiet region, specifically at coordinates (N14W47). By analyzing the 304 Å emission from the SDO/AIIMS telescope, we identified a prominent, large-scale magnetic loop exhibiting a sausage mode oscillation. This loop, which spans approximately 100 Mm, is situated in a strong magnetic field of about 1.2 G. The oscillation's period and decay rate were found to be independent of the noise storm's intensity and size, indicating these factors do not influence the mode's evolution. However, the amplitude of the oscillation scales with the noise storm's magnitude; consequently, the study's findings suggest that the primary driver for the sausage mode is the acoustic wave generated by the noise storm itself.

We present a compact, planar-integrated configuration for a magneto-optical trap (MOT) utilizing micro-fabricated waveguide lasers and a micro-coil for the magnetic field. This design offers a streamlined, space-efficient solution for trapping and cooling atoms, specifically demonstrating the successful trapping of Rubidium-87. The planar layout enhances efficiency by minimizing the propagation distance for resonant light, thereby increasing the effective optical density within the trap. Additionally, the small volume of the micro-fluidic channels housing the atoms allows for precise control of the atomic cloud's spatial density.

The question of why supermassive black holes like Sgr A* and M87* exhibit such low luminosities remains unresolved. We propose a solution to this "luminosity paradox" by suggesting that these black holes are surrounded by a dense, dusty torus. This dusty structure would absorb the radiation from the accretion flow, rendering the black hole's luminosity effectively dim. We demonstrate that this scenario is consistent with recent observations of M87* and Sgr A* obtained from the Event Horizon Telescope.

We examine the spontaneous emission of a 3D-neutral atom in free space and when positioned near a mirror, focusing on how the atom's motion influences this process. By employing a quantized electromagnetic field within the dipole approximation, we derive the density matrix for both stationary and moving atoms. Our analysis demonstrates that for a neutral atom in motion, the presence of the mirror alters the characteristics of the emitted photon compared to emission in free space. Furthermore, we calculate the total radiated power using Fermi's Golden Rule and find that, to first order, this power remains independent of the mirror's properties for both moving and stationary atoms.

We present the first comprehensive analysis of the young massive Westerlund 2 cluster (Wd 2) using *Gaia* DR2 data, which includes 1,062 sources. By applying a rigorous statistical approach, we identify 1,042 cluster members and 20 non-members. Our distance estimate of 1.15 kPa aligns closely with previous studies. We determine the cluster's age to be 2.5 ± 0.5 Myr, a value derived from the turn-off point of the main sequence. Additionally, we calculate the cluster's mass function, finding a slope of $\alpha = 1.35$ for stars with masses below 1 $M_{\odot}$ and a shallower slope of $\alpha = 1.05$ for more massive objects. We also estimate the total cluster mass at 2,600 $M_{\odot}$ and its radius at 2.9 pc. Our findings indicate that Wd 2 is a compact system with a high stellar density, comparable to other clusters of similar age. We also explore the cluster's dynamical history, noting that its mass distribution is centrally concentrated, a feature likely caused by dynamical interactions. Finally, we investigate the ejection of massive stars, estimating an ejection efficiency of 10% based on the observed O and B stars. These results suggest that the cluster's formation was influenced by external factors

This study introduces a variation of the minimax principle designed for addressing specific variational problems that may lack traditional geometric structures. Utilizing this framework, the authors demonstrate the existence of at least one solution to a given problem. Furthermore, the principle is applied to a problem concerning the Dirichlet boundary value for the fractional $p$-Laplacian within $\mathbb{R}^N$.

We introduce a new methodology for restoring degraded document images by integrating a handwritten character recognizer with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The proposed pipeline initially transcribes the source image using a handwritten text recognition model. Subsequently, GANs synthesize a cleaner version of the document by generating text around each recognized word. The input image and its corresponding synthesized version are aligned to create synchronized pairs of reference and synthesized data. The training process involves two phases: first, GANs are trained to generate text for pristine documents using only the recognized words; second, the same GANs are trained on the image-synthesis pairs to produce high-fidelity restored documents. The efficacy of this approach is validated through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating significant improvements over current state-of-the-art methods.

This paper introduces a new dataset comprising ID card images alongside their extracted textual information in various languages, specifically developed to evaluate cross-lingual Optical Character Recognition (OCR) text extraction performance. We further present an efficient pipeline that leverages Natural Language Processing (NLP) to enhance the accuracy of this OCR extraction process.

Channel estimation is critical for maintaining reliable communication in high-mobity environments, yet traditional methods often struggle due to rapid parameter changes. To address this, we introduce an innovative channel estimation technique leveraging the recurrent capabilities of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. By utilizing the temporal dependencies inherent in the received signals, our proposed approach significantly enhances estimation accuracy compared to standard methods, particularly under severe line-of-sight (LoS) conditions.

We have developed a deep learning framework based on generative adversarial networks (GANs) to restore and enhance low-resolution astronomical images. This approach was specifically applied to synthetic data representing the Galactic Center, aiming to create high-fidelity images at 1024x1024 pixels with a 0.01 arcsecond resolution. The resulting images highlight fine details of the region's stellar population and compact sources, achieving a peak dynamic range of 10^6.

This study introduces a new algorithm designed to synthesize high-resolution (HR) images from low-resolution (LR) inputs using neural networks. The proposed method employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) to map LR images directly into their HR counterparts. To prevent overfitting during training, the architecture incorporates a multi-scale structure alongside a data augmentation strategy. For evaluation, the system was tested using the standard LR-HR face pair datasets, and the results were compared against existing methods. The study concludes that the proposed approach achieves superior performance in image quality metrics.

The Early Career Researcher's (ECFR) panel, dedicated to advancing the interests of young scientists within the European Committee for Future Accelerators (ECFA), was formally established in 2019. This document chronicles the group's inaugural year, highlighting the formation of working parties, the organization of an ECFA Young Physicists' Meeting, and the production of an ECYA Position Statement on career pathways. Furthermore, it outlines the group's strategic plan for 2020–2022 and offers recommendations for future ECFA panels.

This study introduces a graphene-based line-wave propagation mechanism in the optical regime, achieved through a specific arrangement of a graphene section flanked by two silicon waveguides. The configuration functions as a linear beam splitter, generating line waves that radiate from the edges of the graphene area. Numerical simulations indicate that the dimensions of the graphene patch critically govern the spectral characteristics of these line waves. Furthermore, the system demonstrates sensitivity to polarized line waves, enabling their effective detection.

This paper introduces a new framework for investigating multi-agent interactions involving both humans and robots through a collaborative setup of four dual-arm robots and two users. By employing a federated learning (FL) approach, the system enables the simultaneous training of a motion planning algorithm across all scenarios without exchanging raw data, thereby preserving data privacy. We outline the methodology for executing experiments within this environment and present initial findings that compare standard versus federated training outcomes.

A novel estimator for the average treatment effect on treated units is introduced, offering robustness to first-order smooth biases in its first stage and achieving second-order smoothness through bias correction. Leveraging high-dimensional estimation techniques, this approach accommodates scenarios where the number of covariates is large relative to the sample size. Simulation studies and an empirical analysis of a real dataset are provided to demonstrate its effectiveness.

Knowledge graph (KG) link prediction aims to infer missing connections between entities by leveraging a variety of data sources. This study introduces a novel attention-based recurrent attention network (A-RAN) for predicting these links, which uniquely integrates information derived from the joint extraction of relations and mentions from unstructured text. Specifically, the proposed method utilizes a joint extraction framework to identify KG mentions and relations within text segments, subsequently employing the resulting model outputs to enhance the links' prediction performance.

We examine the QCD phase diagram within the framework of the Polyloop model, specifically investigating how the transition between hadronic matter and quark matter responds to a rising baryonic chemical potential. Our findings indicate that this transition is of a second-order nature. Furthermore, we determine the Debye mass for both light quarks and di-baryons, observing that they maintain distinct values even when the system reaches the critical point. Finally, we analyze the impact of the quark mass on the phase diagram, noting that the quark mass influences the critical value of the baryonic chemical potential.

The magnetic properties of Tb$_3$RuO$_7$ and Nd$_3$RuO$_7$ were examined using neutron diffraction. In Tb$_3$RuO$_7$, Ru1 and Ru2 ions exhibit opposite magnetic moments, resulting in a double-$\mathbf{k}$ structure, whereas in Nd$_3$RuO$_7$, the moments for Ru1 and Ru2 are parallel, forming a single-$\mathbf{k}$ structure. The observed magnetic ordering in both compounds is attributed to the competition between interplane and intraplane exchange interactions.

We introduce a local-functional framework that maps low-dimensional signals into a high-dimensional space, enabling the learning of a regression function within a Hilbert Space of the functions. This approach offers a theoretical advantage by ensuring that the resulting classifier or regressor generalizes effectively, even when training data is scarce. Furthermore, the framework supports the integration of side information through specific constraints on the functions. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method in the context of regression tasks using graphical side information.

This study introduces a novel framework for multi-task causal modeling that integrates causal knowledge with the target variables themselves. The proposed hybrid model, termed SESYGE, combines the target variables with their underlying causal causes and effects into a single vector. By adopting a semi-generative approach, it treats the components as partially observed data, utilizing information from all three elements to enhance learning. The generative component of SESYGE aims to reconstruct the full set of causal variables and target targets based on available data. The second component, a discriminative layer, analyzes these relationships to explicitly capture causal structures. The third element, a classifier, predicts the target variables directly. The proposed SESYGE framework is validated through experiments on both synthetic datasets and real-world applications, demonstrating its efficacy.

Recent research into deep learning's computational geometry has revealed that specific geometric patterns within these models are not merely incidental but are crucial for their outstanding performance. Grasping this spatial layout can significantly inform the refinement of both algorithmic strategies and system architectures in the domain. This study investigates the geometric properties of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by examining their internal representations of image data. We analyze how these features are organized across different layers and channels, specifically evaluating the convolutional kernels' sensitivity to spatial shifts and the structural relationships between feature maps. The findings demonstrate that CNNs encode a consistent geometric framework representing the image plane, a property that persists regardless of the network's composition, including variations in kernel dimensions, image scale, and architectural design. Furthermore, this internal geometry mirrors the external arrangement of receptive fields, effectively constituting the model's representation of the image domain.

This research examines the distribution of lattice minima within cubic fields, a concept rooted in the work of Minkowski. We demonstrate that selecting specific radicands can cause lattice points to either accumulate or disperse, a phenomenon that may be explained by a family of lower bounds for lattice values derived from the theory of theta functions. Additionally, we investigate the impact of varying the cubic shape parameter on lattice behavior and provide numerical evidence supporting a conjecture by P. Pollack regarding the maximization of lattice values in totally real fields through totally real signatures.

Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) serves as a method for assigning relevance to inputs to interpret deep neural network (DNN) predictions. This study examines LRP's ability to reveal the characteristics of DNNs by analyzing its effects on MNIST and CIFAR-10 image classification models. We evaluate the generated relevance maps across various network architectures and examine how the choice of numerical epsilon influences the resulting interpretations.

We introduce a generalized form of the $r$-associated Stirling number of the second kind, defined by the constraint that every subset in a partition of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ has a cardinality of at least $r$. This definition extends the traditional concept, where $r$ is fixed, by treating it as a variable. Our analysis includes determining their fundamental properties, establishing recurrence relations applicable to various scenarios, and exploring their generating functions.

Irreducible domains within layered materials are defined by their minimal non-contractible symmetries. This study outlines a methodology for classifying these domains by mapping them directly to the finite double cosets of the $B_n$ Coxeter group. This approach leverages the identification of such domains as the minimal symmetries in systems exhibiting symmetry-breaking phase transitions. As a specific illustration, the work derives a universal framework for ordering in hexagonal and honeyhexagonal layers, thereby unifying and extending prior research on irreducible domains in graphene and similar structures.

We demonstrate that on any compact Riemannian manifold $M$ with diameter $D$, the cutoff for achievable momentum resolution, denoted as $p_{\rm max}$, corresponds to a de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_{\rm dB}$ that is at least as large as $D$ ($\lambda_{\rm dB} \ge D$). This constraint imposes a fundamental limit on the precision with which a quantum state can be characterized, suggesting that the physical description of localized systems is inherently "fuzzy." Specifically, for a system confined to a region of size $L$, its momentum distribution must extend beyond $L/hbar$, rendering the concept of a sharply localized point incompatible with quantum mechanics.

Flow-based generative models offer a viable solution for sampling from high-dimensional distributions, yet their reliance on Monte Carlo (MC) integration often restricts practical use due to slow convergence and elevated computational costs. This study introduces a framework that leverages complex-val affine coupling layers to enhance the efficiency of these MC simulations. By incorporating complex-valued operations, we achieve greater numerical stability, thereby allowing for a substantial reduction in the number of MC samples necessary for accurate convergence. Empirical results across various benchmarks demonstrate that our approach significantly accelerates the generation of samples from challenging, high-dimensional target distributions.

This work presents a bottom-quark Yukawa coupling framework based on U(1)$_F$ flavor symmetry breaking, aiming to explain the vast top-to-bottom quark mass disparity. In our model, the bottom quark arises from the mixing of two distinct bottom-like states associated with different U(1)$_F$ charges. The resulting mass hierarchy emerges from the suppression of the bottom-like state's Yukawa coupling by a symmetry-breaking scale, while the top quark's mass is generated via the mixing of top and charm quarks. This mechanism naturally suppresses the Yukawa couplings of the $c$ and $t$ quarks. Consequently, the model predicts a bottom quark mass that aligns with experimental measurements and forecasts a bottom-to-top mass ratio of approximately $10^{-4}$, which is consistent with the observed ratio.

Virtual Platform Performance Monitoring Counters (VPPMs) are frequently employed to track hardware utilization and support applications ranging from power management to cloud resource allocation. However, their potential for malicious exploitation remains largely unexplored. This study investigates how VPPMs can facilitate side-channel attacks within virtualized settings, enabling attackers to breach security protocols, steal sensitive data, or evade detection. We introduce a novel attack methodology that combines VPPM data with a custom virtualized side-channel to compromise cryptographic keys, demonstrating successful key extraction from both AES and RSA algorithms. Additionally, we detail an attack leveraging VPPMs to bypass virtualized security boundaries, allowing the circumvention of hypervisor-based safeguards.

Recent years have seen the development of zero-shot translation using large-scale multilingual pre-trained models. This study investigates the factors underlying the adaptability of such models to entirely new, unseen languages. Specifically, we introduce "ProtoTrans," a cross-lingual pre-training framework designed to assess linguistic similarity by identifying a prototype sentence for each target language based on its bar-centric embedding. By training ProtoTrans on a diverse set of 200 languages, we can determine the most suitable language prototype—and by extension, the most appropriate pre-trained model—for any language not originally present in the dataset. Experiments conducted on 200 under-resourced languages reveal that this approach successfully predicts which existing pre-trained language yields the best zero-shot translation performance for novel targets.

Rotating stellar cores are frequently modeled as isolated, axisymmetric, steady, and slowly varying systems in both compressible and incompressible fluid dynamics. This study utilizes direct numerical simulations of a compressible, rotating, stratified fluid to explore the stability of such cores, specifically examining the influence of rotation on baroclinic instability. The analysis focuses on the stability of basic states that are baroclinic, rotating, and stratified, with particular attention to the impact of rotation on baroclinic instability. The findings indicate that the binary mass in a rotating core tends to increase as the ratio of kinetic to gravitational energy rises. The study also examines the stability of these configurations, showing that the binary mass is not solely determined by the ratio of kinetic to gravitational energy.
